# 📦 @knopki/dsh-prompt-profiles
Per-session prompt profiles for DeepSeek Harness: reusable system-prompt sections, grouped into name
d profiles, sealed into the session prompt

🇬🇧 English •
🇷🇺 Русский •
🇨🇳 中文
🗄️ Archived. Issues and pull requests are closed along with the repository. Fork it if you still nee
d it: MIT, and lib/ is committed, so a fork installs without a build.
➡️ Want another agent voice? Use an agent preset with @deepseek-ai/dsh-persona. The migration sectio
n below is the whole recipe.
> **This repository is archived.** Read-only: no further releases, no issue triage. The plugin still
works on the DSH release it targets, but the problem it solves is now covered by the platform itsel
f. Read why and how to get the same result without it. The reference documentation below stays for a
nyone still running an installed copy.
## Why it is archived
**The platform grew the same axis.** This bundle added a "how the agent is told to work" dimension n
ext to agent presets. Agent presets have since become the first-party home for exactly that: `@deeps
eek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` declares an agent's child rows as ordinary YAML, and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-pers
ona` owns the persona prefix and suffix slots inside a preset. One preset per voice does what one pr
ofile did, and it does it through the platform's own loader, prompt registry, and documentation inst
ead of a second implementation of each.
**What that buys over this plugin.** The bundle has to shadow the assembled prompt, keep sealed per-
session snapshots under `$DSH_HOME/storages/prompt_profiles/`, and write its own definition rows int
o `cordis.patch.yml`. It also pins a peer window (`>=0.1.7-rc.2 <0.2.2-0`) and needs `dsh plugin all
ow-version` outside it, and it injects two client packages to draw the composer chip and the editor.
A preset composition declares the package it mounts and nothing else: no version exemption, no stor
age to reap, no client injection, and the persona text sits in the same YAML block as the tools and
permissions it goes with, so "what the agent is" and "how it is told to work" are read and reviewed
t goes with, so "what the agent is" and "how it is told to work" are read and reviewed in one place.
**It found no users.** The npm registry reports zero downloads for the package, and the only install
ation I know of is mine. A bundle nobody installs costs a re-verification pass on every DSH release
window and returns nothing. Archiving is the honest outcome; a fork is one `git clone` away if you d
nd returns nothing. Archiving is the honest outcome; a fork is one `git clone` away if you disagree.
### 1. Inventory what you actually have
Profiles and sections live as rows in your profile composition (`cordis.patch.yml` for a web profile
, `~/.dsh/cordis.patch.yml` for a shared install), under the `prompt-profiles` insert row. Read them
out before deleting anything, or open **Settings → Prompt profiles → Preview**, which shows each pr
ofile in position among the built-in sections — that ordering is what the preset has to reproduce.
### 3. Reproduce what `scope` was doing
This is the one place the mapping is not mechanical. A prompt-profiles section could be `inherit`, `
main-only`, or `subagents-only`; a preset has no per-section scope, it has one composition. Text tha
t only ever addressed subagents belongs in a preset those subagents are created with, not in the par
ent's persona — whether that is convenient depends on how you spawn them. If neither split suits you
, folding the text into the parent persona is the pragmatic answer, and a subagent simply reads guid
ance it does not act on.
### What the migration loses
- The editor: profile and section lists, drag-and-drop ordering, in-place preview among built-in sec

tions, search, debounced autosave, three UI languages.
- Reuse: a section referenced by five profile
s was one string with five placements. A preset inlines its own text; share it with a YAML anchor or

duplicate it.
- The composer chip and its per-workspace memory, including the explicit `None` decis

ion.
- Per-section scope.
Not lost: sealing. A preset fixes an agent's composition when the agent is created and is not retrof
itted into a live one, so the "start a new session to apply it" behavior carries over unchanged.
## Overview
`@knopki/dsh-prompt-profiles` adds a second axis to a DeepSeek Harness profile. Agent presets decide
what an agent is: which tools and behaviors are available. Prompt profiles decide how that agent is
told to work. The same agent with the same tools can run as a terse reviewer or as a specialist tha
t follows a house style, and the only thing that changes is the profile you pick at session start.
A profile is an ordered list of references to reusable sections. Every reference carries its own pos
ition and scope, so a single section can appear in several profiles in a different place each time.
The profile is chosen when a session starts, sealed into that session's prompt, and never revised af
terwards. Choose no profile and the system prompt is not modified at all.
The editor and the composer chip live in the web GUI, so you build profiles without hand-editing a s
ingle prompt string.
## Requirements
- DSH in `>=0.1.7-rc.2 <0.2.2-0` — the peer window this bundle declares; `0.2.1-alpha.2` is the rele

ase it is verified on.
- Outside that window DSH disables the plugin until you grant it the exact-ve

rsion exemption (`dsh plugin allow-version`).
- The installed profile's own plugins: on the host `se
ttings`, `configEditor`, `workspaceRegistry`, `storageDomain`, `typert` and `agentPresets`; on the w
eb client `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-settings`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-conversation` and `@dee

pseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives`.
- A missing optional service degrades one feature. It does not b

ient-ui-primitives`.
- A missing optional service degrades one feature. It does not block the mount.
## Known limitations
- One DSH process. Writes from a single DSH process are coordinated; a second DSH process editing th

e same profile patch can overwrite rows or choices.
- Strict sealing. A session's decision is made o
nce and never revised, an empty decision included. A session that started before its snapshot record
existed keeps its result, so start a new session to get a profile into it.
